subject: pathology
title: Plasma cell neoplasms, histiocytic disorders and spleen

steps.tx: **Plasma cell neoplasms** range from MGUS through smouldering myeloma to active multiple myeloma with organ damage over time. MGUS stays below ten percent marrow plasma cells and causes no end organ injury during careful observation periods. Active myeloma produces **CRAB features**, which include hypercalcaemia, renal failure, anaemia and destructive bone lesions in patients. A monoclonal spike with abnormal **free light chain ratio** tracks the clone at every stage of disease.
steps.say: Plasma cell neoplasms are disorders where clonal plasma cells expand from incidental MGUS towards symptomatic myeloma over years progressively. CRAB features appear because calcium rises while kidneys fail and bones develop destructive lesions in active disease stages. Monoclonal protein helps clinicians track clone burden during treatment and later relapse monitoring.

steps.tx: **Multiple myeloma** fills marrow with clonal plasma cells that secrete monoclonal immunoglobulin or free light chains continuously. Light chains precipitate inside renal tubules as casts and cause **myeloma kidney**, while osteoclast activation punches lytic lesions into bones. Red cells stack into **rouleaux** because abnormal proteins coat their surfaces, and normal antibody suppression causes recurrent bacterial infections. Bone pain, anaemia and renal failure therefore form a classic combination in older patients presenting late.
steps.say: Multiple myeloma is a cancer where clonal plasma cells secrete light chains that obstruct renal tubules as casts internally. Lytic lesions develop because osteoclast activation destroys bone without forming a reactive sclerotic rim around lesions visibly. Rouleaux formation occurs because abnormal proteins coat red cells and stack them together.

steps.tx: **Waldenstrom macroglobulinaemia** is a lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma that secretes monoclonal IgM into blood in large pentameric molecules continuously. That IgM increases viscosity and causes visual disturbance, bleeding and neuropathy because blood flows sluggishly through small vessels everywhere. Unlike myeloma, lytic bone lesions stay absent while **hyperviscosity** dominates the presentation and requires urgent plasmapheresis when symptomatic. **AL amyloidosis** can complicate any light chain clone by depositing misfolded protein in heart and kidney tissues.
steps.say: Waldenstrom disease is a lymphoma where monoclonal IgM thickens blood and impairs flow through small vessels throughout body tissues. Hyperviscosity symptoms develop because pentameric IgM molecules sludge circulation in retina, brain and mucosa noticeably during disease progression. Plasmapheresis helps clinicians remove IgM rapidly when vision becomes threatened by severe hyperviscosity.

left.title: MGUS
points: M protein under 30 g/L, marrow plasma cells under 10 percent

right.title: Multiple myeloma
points: Clonal plasma cells 10 percent plus with CRAB or biomarkers
Lytic lesions, renal casts, anaemia, calcium
Treat with proteasome, IMiD and antibody regimens

steps.tx: The **spleen** enlarges through congestion, increased workload, infiltration or malignancy depending on the underlying systemic disease process involved. Portal hypertension congests the spleen, haemolysis increases its workload, and lymphoma or myelofibrosis infiltrates its tissue directly over time. Loss of splenic function risks overwhelming infection from encapsulated organisms because filtering and opsonisation fail after splenectomy or autosplenectomy. **Howell Jolly bodies** appear on blood films afterwards because nuclear remnants are no longer removed efficiently.
steps.say: Splenomegaly is a sign where congestion, haemolysis, infiltration or malignancy enlarges the spleen through different systemic mechanisms depending on disease. Splenic loss is dangerous because encapsulated bacteria escape filtering and cause overwhelming sepsis in asplenic patients rapidly without warning signs. Howell Jolly bodies appear because nuclear remnants persist when splenic filtering disappears.

steps.tx: **Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis** occurs when activated macrophages engulf blood cells during an uncontrolled inflammatory response triggered by infection or lymphoma. Ferritin rises extremely high while cytopenias deepen because marrow and peripheral cells become consumed by activated macrophages everywhere. **Langerhans cell histiocytosis** produces lytic skull lesions, rash and diabetes insipidus in children through clonal dendritic cell proliferation locally. Its cells contain Birbeck granules shaped like tennis rackets under electron microscopy in classic descriptions.
steps.say: Haemophagocytic disease is a syndrome where activated macrophages consume blood cells during uncontrolled inflammation triggered by infection or lymphoma underlying disease. Ferritin rises dramatically because macrophage activation releases inflammatory mediators throughout marrow and reticuloendothelial tissues in severely ill patients systematically. Trigger control helps clinicians stop consumption while supportive care stabilises cytopenias.

steps.tx: This histology shows large pale cells with grooved coffee bean nuclei surrounded by bright orange red **eosinophils** in tissue. The brown inset confirms **CD1a and langerin positivity**, which identifies these abnormal cells as Langerhans cells rather than ordinary macrophages. That combination diagnoses **Langerhans cell histiocytosis**, a clonal disorder that causes lytic bone lesions, rash and diabetes insipidus in children. Examiners use this image because nuclear grooves, eosinophils and immunostaining converge on one classic diagnosis.
steps.say: This histology shows grooved nuclei because Langerhans cells fold their nuclear membrane into a coffee bean shape characteristically under microscopy. Eosinophils appear alongside them because the lesion recruits bright orange inflammatory cells around the clonal dendritic cells locally within tissue sections. Immunostaining helps clinicians confirm lineage when CD1a and langerin stain strongly positive.
